time_scope: modern Tongan; four native speakers aged 25-50 in acoustic study
claim: Definitive accent is a noun-phrase-level phenomenon rather than a property of the noun itself: prominence is realized on the final word of the relevant NP even when that word is an adjective rather than the noun.

examples: ko e ika kulokula 'the red fish'
ko e ika kulokula lalahi 'the big red fish'

normalized_environment: DEFINITIVE_ACCENT targets RIGHT_EDGE(NP), not lexical noun
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Examples are wide-focus NPs; authors explicitly note they do not illustrate narrow adjective focus.

claim: Definitive accent independently lengthens the final vowel: vowels with DA averaged about 1.65 times the duration of vowels without DA (284 vs 172 ms). The effect interacts with phonemic length: DA nearly doubles short vowels (~1.95x) but increases long vowels by about 30% (~1.3x), and short+DA vowels are not significantly different in duration from long unaccented vowels.
normalized_environment: DEFINITIVE_ACCENT adds duration at NP right edge; magnitude conditioned by PHONEMIC_LENGTH
exceptions_or_counterexamples: DA does not add a uniform absolute/relative duration across short and long vowels; length interaction is significant.
section: 4.2 Effect of Definitive Accent on Duration in NPs; 4.4 Duration Summary

claim: Pitch maxima support invariant penultimate-mora stress: in words without definitive accent, the pitch peak occurred near the beginning of the penultimate mora in 100% of examined cases; under definitive accent, interpreting the added duration as vowel gemination preserves the same penultimate-mora alignment.

source_forms.without_DA: pitch peak near beginning of penultimate mora in 100% of examined cases
source_forms.short_DA: relative pitch-peak location not significantly changed, p=.5175
source_forms.long_DA: pitch-peak location shifts as added duration precedes peak; p<.0001

formal_environment: Stress -> penultimate mora; F0 peak aligned near beginning of stressed mora
normalized_environment: PRIMARY_STRESS invariantly PENULTIMATE_MORA; DA changes quantity rather than stress rule
scope: acoustic target words in VP/AP/NP contexts
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Long vowels with DA show shifted proportional peak location because extra duration is added; authors interpret this as compatible with constant mora-counted stress rather than an exception.

claim: Outside definitive accent, phonologically long target vowels averaged twice the duration of short vowels (246 vs 123 ms, p<.0001). Stress did not significantly change long-vowel duration, whereas stressed short vowels were about 1.3 times as long as unstressed shorts.
formal_environment: V duration conditioned by phonemic length and stress
normalized_environment: LONG_VOWEL ≈ 2x SHORT_VOWEL; STRESS lengthening primarily affects SHORT vowels
exceptions_or_counterexamples: No significant stress-duration effect for long vowels in this dataset; stress is more reliably cued by pitch than duration.
section: 4.1 Effects of Vowel Length and Stress on Duration in VPs and APs
